text: The applicant was born in 1986.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant lives in Mozhaysk, Moscow Region.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 31 January 2009, the applicant and six other people decided to hold a flash mob in front of the Office of the Russian Government in Moscow.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant and six other people arrived at the Office of the Russian Government in Moscow at around 1 p.m. on 31 January 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant and six other people positioned themselves at Gorbatyy Bridge on 31 January 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Each participant in the flash mob held a blank sheet of paper.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Each participant in the flash mob had their mouth covered with adhesive tape.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At 1.20 p.m. on 31 January 2009, the police ordered the group at Gorbatyy Bridge to disperse.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant asked to be informed of the grounds for the police order to disperse.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was taken to Presnenskiy police station.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was charged under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (breaches of the established procedure for the organisation or conduct of public gatherings, meetings, demonstrations, marches or pickets).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The charge against the applicant under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences related to his participation in a public gathering.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The basis for the charge against the applicant was that the requirement of prior notification under the Federal Law on Gatherings, Meetings, Demonstrations, Processions and Pickets, no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), had not been respected.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 11 March 2009, the justice of the peace of the 378th circuit of the Presnenskiy District of Moscow convicted the applicant of the administrative offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace of the 378th circuit of the Presnenskiy District of Moscow sentenced the applicant to a fine of 1,000 Russian roubles (approximately 22 euros).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The judgment of 11 March 2009 stated that at 1.20 p.m. on 31 January 2009, the applicant, as a participant in the public event in the form of a static demonstration (пикетирование), breached the established procedure for the conduct of a public event.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant denied his guilt in respect of the administrative offence charged under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant stated that he had been aware of the need to comply with the notification procedure when organising a public event.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant stated that in this particular case compliance with the notification procedure had not been necessary because the act had not been political in character but had been a flash mob, that is to say a synchronised action of several people.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant told the police officers that the participants in the act had not been involved in a public event but had been taking photos on Gorbatyy Bridge while holding blank sheets of paper.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace of the 378th circuit of the Presnenskiy District of Moscow declined the applicant's arguments because his guilt in the administrative offence had been proved by the bulk of evidence examined in the course of the court hearing.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The judgment of 11 March 2009 found that the applicant voluntarily and directly participated in the public event in the form of a static demonstration that had been taking place in breach of the procedure set out by the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The judgment of 11 March 2009 found that the applicant failed to comply with the lawful order by the police officers to stop the static demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The justice of the peace of the 378th circuit of the Presnenskiy District of Moscow dismissed the applicant's argument that the act did not amount to a public event in the form of a static demonstration and that he did not participate in a public event, because the evidence collected in the case showed otherwise.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant appealed against the judgment of 11 March 2009, challenging the applicability of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) to the circumstances of the case.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant appealed against the judgment of 11 March 2009, contesting the fine imposed on him.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 28 April 2009, the Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow upheld the judgment of 11 March 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow dismissed the applicant's and his lawyer's arguments presented in the statement of appeal.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant appeared at around 2 p.m. on 31 January 2009 among a group of comrades with whom he had agreed to do so on the Internet, on the bridge in front of the building at 2 Krasnopresnenskaya Embankment in Moscow.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant covered his mouth with adhesive tape during the event on 31 January 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant carried sheets of A4 paper without any inscriptions or images during the event on 31 January 2009.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant was present for ten to fifteen minutes at the bridge in front of the building at 2 Krasnopresnenskaya Embankment in Moscow in the absence of any permission whatsoever.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant's actions fully met the criteria of the administrative offence set out in Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences in the form of a static demonstration.

text: A summary of the relevant domestic law and practice can be found in Kasparov and Others v. Russia (no. 21613/07, § 35, 3 October 2013).
A summary of the relevant domestic law and practice can be found in Navalnyy and Yashin v. Russia (no. 76204/11, §§ 43-44, 4 December 2014).
A summary of the relevant domestic law and practice can be found in Novikova and Others v. Russia (nos. 25501/07 and 4 others, §§ 67-69, 26 April 2016).
A summary of the relevant domestic law and practice can be found in Lashmankin and Others v. Russia (nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, §§ 216-312, 7 February 2017).
The provisions of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) as in force at the material time directly relevant to the present case are set out in the judgment.

Section 2(1) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) defined a 'public event' as an open, peaceful event accessible to all, organised at the initiative of citizens of the Russian Federation, political parties, other public associations, or religious associations.

Section 2(1) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) provided that a public event must have the aims of expressing or developing opinions freely and voicing demands on issues related to political, economic, social or cultural life in the country, and issues related to foreign policy.

The Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) distinguished between five types of public event: a gathering (собрание); a meeting (митинг); a demonstration (демонстрация); a march (шествие); and a static demonstration (пикетирование).

Further details on the five types of public event under the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) can be found in Lashmankin and Others v. Russia (nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, § 219, 7 February 2017).

Section 2(6) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) defined a static demonstration as a form of public expression of opinion that does not involve movement or the use of loudspeaker equipment.

Section 2(6) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) provided that in a static demonstration, one or more citizens with placards, banners and other means of visual expression station themselves near the target object of the static demonstration.

In accordance with sections 5(4)(1) and 7(1)(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification in respect of a static demonstration involving several persons must be submitted no later than three days before the intended static demonstration.

In accordance with sections 5(4)(1) and 7(1)(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), if the end of the notification time-limit falls on a Sunday or a public holiday, notification must be submitted no later than four days before the intended static demonstration.
Under the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), no notification was required for gatherings (собрание).
Under the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), no notification was required for static demonstrations involving one person.
In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the purpose of a public event.
In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the form of a public event.
In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the place of a public event.
In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the date and the time of the beginning and ending of a public event.
In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the envisioned number of participants of a public event.

In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the methods by employing which the organiser of a public event intends to ensure that public order be maintained and emergency medical aid be made available.

In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the full name of the organiser of a public event, his or her address and phone number.

In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the full names of persons authorised by the organiser of a public event to represent him or her in the course of a public event.
In accordance with section 7(3) of the Public Events Act (Federal Law no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), notification must contain the date of submitting the notification.
